# Roy Gardner

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v3 c25 P35](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0035), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v3 c25 P35](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0035), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Roy  <sub>[v3 c25 P43](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0043), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>

## Appearance

Roy is an adorably handsome youth with courtly manners, a classic nose, and glorious, dreamy dark eyes. He is well-gowned and has a deep, dark, velvety smile.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P56](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0056), [v3 c25 P35](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0035), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c38 P44](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0044)_

## Personality

Roy is polite, romantic, and clever, with a soft-spoken, pleading voice and a habit of paying elaborate compliments and writing poetry. Despite his dramatic and courtly charm, he entirely lacks a sense of humor and is described as being uninteresting underneath his attractive exterior.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c38 P44](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0044), [v3 c38 P45](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0045), [v3 c39 P2](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0002)_

## History

Royal Gardner was a student at Redmond College whose studies were interrupted for two years when he accompanied his ill mother abroad. Upon returning to college, he met Anne Shirley in a park during a rainstorm by rescuing her with his umbrella and subsequently sent her flowers. Over the next two years at Redmond, he courted Anne devotedly, sending her poems, orchids, and violets, and introducing her to his family. After graduating from Redmond, he proposed to Anne in the harbor park pavilion where they had first met. When Anne realized she did not love him and refused his proposal, he expressed bitterness before parting from her. His sister Dorothy later noted that he was recovering from the heartbreak, as he had from previous romantic disappointments.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P35](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0035), [v3 c25 P42](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0042), [v3 c25 P44](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0044), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c36 P17](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0017), [v3 c36 P24](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0024), [v3 c37 P30](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0030), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017), [v3 c38 P18](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0018), [v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027), [v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032), [v3 c39 P4](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0004), [v3 c39 P6](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0006)_

## Background by volume

- Son of a deceased father and a wealthy mother  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Belongs to one of the rich, prominent families in Kingsport  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Had to leave college to travel abroad with his sick mother for two years  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Had fallen in love twice before meeting Anne Shirley  <sub>[v3 c39 P6](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0006)</sub>

## Quotes

> We are schoolmates, I see. That ought to be sufficient introduction. My name is Royal Gardner. And you are the Miss Shirley who read the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic the other evening, aren’t you?  <sub>[v3 c25 P36](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0036)</sub>

> So you’ve just been amusing yourself these two years?  <sub>[v3 c38 P25](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0025)</sub>

> You have ruined my life,  <sub>[v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027)</sub>

> You can give me no hope?  <sub>[v3 c38 P30](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0030)</sub>

> Then—good-bye. I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne.  <sub>[v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032)</sub>
